issues.title: Operative Status Clarification
issues.author: sbarguil
issues.body:
Understanding the interrelationships between the operational status of VPN services, VPN nodes, and VPN network access is another significant operational gap. The status of a VPN service may depend on the status of the underlying VPN nodes and the network access provided to the VPN.

To address this gap, IETF should establish clear dependencies and correlations between the various operational statuses. This could involve defining specific criteria for determining the overall status of a VPN service based on the status of its constituent VPN nodes and network access components. Moreover, real-time monitoring and correlation of status information can provide insights into the health and performance of VPN services.

comments.author: sbarguil
comments.body:
see also, https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/onions/if1BRJpZqNNxcemra8sq8yz-FBQ/

> From: Alexander Vainshtein <Alexander.Vainshtein=40rbbn.com@dmarc.ietf.org<
> 
> I have looked up the standard and found that it presumably mentions Operational Status of a pseudowire as oper-status without any clarifications and/or references, and, specifically, without any association with various indicators in the PW Status TLV.
> 
> This is quite different from RFC [5601<https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5601>](http://5601%3Chttps//datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5601%3E),  which explicitly provides such linkage as can be seen from the quoted text below:
> 
>   pwOperStatus OBJECT-TYPE
>      SYNTAX        PwOperStatusTC
>      MAX-ACCESS    read-only
>      STATUS        current
>      DESCRIPTION
>           "This object indicates the operational status of the PW; it
>            does not reflect the status of the Customer Edge (CE) bound
>            interface.  It is set to down only if pwNotForwarding,
>            psnFacingPwRxFault, or psnFacingPwTxFault indications are
>            set in pwLocalStatus or pwRemoteStatus.
>            It indicates 'lowerLayerDown' if the only reason for
>            not being in the 'up' state is that either the outer tunnel
>            or physical layer of the network side is in the 'down'
>            state.
>            All other states are declared based on the description
>            of the PwOperStatusTC.
>            "
> 
> I wonder whether, from your POV, the quoted definition of the PW Operatonal Status is still applicable or not.


Regards, and lots of thanks in advance,
Sasha

issues.title: Is the Service running on the Network?
issues.author: sbarguil
issues.body:
How can the northbound system be assured with 100% certainty that a configuration has been successfully installed on the network device?

What mechanisms or feedback loops exist to confirm successful configuration deployment beyond simple acknowledgment?

How does the system can handle transient errors or partial configuration applications from the model perspective?

Are there specific operational attributes that can be used to reflect the real-time status of the configuration?

Does the network element provide any operational state parameters or notifications that indicate whether the configuration is active, pending, or has failed?

If a configuration is manually removed via CLI at the network device, is there a mechanism to reflect this change northbound?

issues.title: L2NM: support for vlan-lists/vlan-ranges
issues.author: sbarguil
issues.body:
When defining a Layer 2 service, sometimes multiple VLANs are mapped into a given service. It would be good to support this in the L2NM encapsulation stanza. 

Examples:

(i) typically used in single-tagged scenarios:
vlan-id-list [ 200 210-219 222 234 240-249 ];


(ii) dual-tagged scenario, with s-vlan=430 and a list of c-vlans:
vlan-tags outer 430 inner-list [ 200 210-219 222 234 240-249 ];

I don't think we need to define tag translate operations for the lists shown above, I have not seen that deployed.

issues.title: L2NM: support for translate-push and pop-translate tag operations
issues.author: sbarguil
issues.body:
I think that in the current version of the L2NM, translate-push and pop-translate are not supported. It would be useful to support them, for example:

translate-push: packet arrives from CE with tag 101. This is swapped for tag 500 and then tag 400 is pushed on top.

pop-translate: packet arrives from CE with tag 100 on top and tag 200 underneath. Tag 100 is popped and tag 200 is swapped for tag 300.

issues.title: No network model for ACLs
issues.author: sbarguil
issues.body:
VPN services often include mechanisms to filter forwarding packets. 

Today, the LxNM models allow to include a 'forwarding-profile-identifier'. A forwarding profile refers to the
 policies that apply to the forwarding of packets conveyed within a      VPN.  Such policies may consist, for example, of applying Access Control Lists (ACLs).

However, currently there is not an ACL network service model (even though a device level ACL model exists).

issues.title: Applicability to Option A, B, C
issues.author: sbarguil
issues.body: this also cover the link with AC models.

comments.author: sbarguil
comments.body:
As part of this effort, we are seeking guidance on how to model and operationalize Inter-AS VPN options (A, B, and C as defined in RFC 4364) using the L3NM framework. While we understand that L3NM provides a service-centric and abstracted model (complementing L3SM), we are particularly interested in how to bridge this abstraction to the specific Inter-AS deployment models in a scalable and standardized way.
 
Our Questions and Clarifications:
 
1. Inter-AS Option A (VRF-to-VRF at ASBR)
In this model, ASBRs behave similarly to PEs, with VRFs on both sides and CE-like links between ASBRs.
Can L3NM model this scenario by treating each ASBR as a site-network-access connecting to a vpn-service, where the remote ASBR is abstracted as a CE?
Are there any attributes (e.g., RTs, routing protocol types) that you would recommend modeling explicitly to support this case?
 
2. Inter-AS Option B (EBGP between ASBRs using VPNv4/v6)
Here, ASBRs perform VPNv4/v6 route exchange via EBGP, and VRFs reside only on PEs.
Does L3NM support modeling such inter-AS ASBR peering relationships directly?
Would it be appropriate to rely on RFC 8345 (Network Topology YANG Model) in conjunction with L3NM to represent AS-level connectivity and the inter-domain peering context?
 
Would you recommend an augmentation or interface between L3NM and a topology model to capture this case effectively?
 
3. Inter-AS Option C (MP-BGP between PEs, ASBRs as MPLS Transit)
This option uses direct MP-BGP sessions between PEs, with ASBRs acting as label-switching transit routers.
Is there a way in L3NM to explicitly model PE-to-PE overlay connections that traverse non-service-aware ASBRs?
Should ASBRs in this case be entirely abstracted from the L3NM model and instead represented within the network topology ?
 
Are there any existing drafts, extensions, or design guidelines currently under consideration for L3NM that address multi-AS or inter-domain VPN service automation?

issues.title: Routing Policies as a List
issues.author: sbarguil
issues.body:
Some devices support the addition of routing policies as list of leaf-list within the VPRN services:

```
configure
  /service vprn VPRN-01
    import-policy-list POL-ALLOW-VOIP
    import-policy-list POL-ALLOW-VIDEO
    import-policy-list POL-DENY-UNKNOWN
    commit

```
Rigth Now the L3NM only handles one policy:

**name** | import-policy| -->type leaf (string)

This will provide greater flexibility and robustness to the implementation.

issues.title: Route-Policy Association Complexity
issues.author: sbarguil
issues.body:
Current RFC 9182 Approach:

Route-policies are associated via vpn-instance-profiles and active-instance-profiles. This indirection adds complexity without clear operational benefit for many deployments. A service provider wants to simply attach a VRF export policy to a VPN site endpoint. With the current model, they must:

1. Define a vpn-instance-profile
2. Configure routing parameters within it
3. Reference it via active-instance-profiles at the vpn-network-access level
4. Manage profile lifecycle separately from the VPN service


Propose a simplified, direct route-policy binding at the vpn-network-access level as an alternative mechanism
This does not require changing the existing model but could be proposed as an optional augmentation or an update to the applicability statement. Operators can directly associate policies to VPN endpoints without managing separate profile lifecycles and reducing configuration steps

issues.title: Lack of Metadata for Route-Policy Applicability
issues.author: sbarguil
issues.body:
Current RFC 9067 Gap

RFC 9067 defines policy-definitions as a flat list with no mechanism to indicate:

Where a policy is intended to be used
Which customer/tenant it belongs to
Which device platforms support it

e.g. A service provider has 500 route-policies.
When an operator provisions a new VPN site for Customer-A and needs to select a VRF export policy, the UI presents all 500 policies. The operator must:

Manually identify which policies belong to Customer-A
Know which policies are valid for VRF export (vs. BGP neighbor or redistribution)
Hope they don't accidentally select CUST-B-VRF-IMPORT for Customer-A's VRF export

Proposed YANG augmentation to RFC 9067 that supports metadata annotations for:
Valid attachment points per policy
Tenant/customer association
Platform constraints
This could be proposed as an informational or standards-track draft extending RFC 9067
